elements.quote: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: Explicitly states the systematic review aim.

elements.quote: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: Clear statement of the main objective.

elements.quote: We included any guideline that provided recommendations on the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19.
elements.reason: Specifies inclusion criteria but not exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: We searched Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, CNKI, CBM, WanFang, and grey literature from November 2019 - November 2020.
elements.reason: Identifies sources and search period.

elements.quote: We assessed the quality with the AGREE II instrument
elements.reason: Specifies method for quality assessment, which includes bias assessment.

elements.quote: We descriptively summarized CPGs characteristics.
elements.reason: Specifies descriptive summary but not detailed synthesis methods.

elements.quote: 71 CPGs were included.
elements.reason: Reports number of included studies but not participants.

elements.quote: Means (Standard Deviations) of the scores for the 6 domains of the AGREE II instrument were 65%(SD19.56%), 39%(SD19.64%), 27%(SD19.48%), 70%(SD15.74%), 26%(SD18.49%), 42%(SD34.91) for the scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigor of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, editorial independence domains, respectively.
elements.reason: Presents results for main outcomes (AGREE II domain scores).
No meta-analysis was conducted, as per descriptive methods.
No groups are compared in the review.
No limitations summarized in the abstract.

elements.quote: Future CPGs for COVID-19 need to rely, for their development, on standard evidence-based methods and tools.
elements.reason: Provides interpretation and implications.
Funding not mentioned in the abstract.
Registration not mentioned in the abstract.

elements.quote: global uncertainty about the natural history of the COVID-19 infection, the lack of direct evidence
elements.reason: Describes important uncertainties in CPG development due to pandemic conditions.

elements.quote: The clinical purpose was to inform the target users in selecting and using trustworthy CPGs in their daily practice. The methodological purpose was to inform and inspire the progress of standardization of the RG development methodologies.
elements.reason: Explains the importance and need for the review for clinical and methodological purposes.

elements.quote: Four previous reviews have assessed the quality of COVID-19 CPGs [16-18]. Two of them focused on the CPGs produced in the early phase of the pandemic. ... However, an assessment of all the CPGs focused on the management of critically ill COVID -19 patients was lacking.
elements.reason: Cites previous reviews and explains the need for the current review to fill the gap.
This review is about the quality of clinical practice guidelines, not intervention effects.
This review does not involve complex interventions or delivery contexts in the sense of the review itself.

elements.quote: Objective: We aimed to systematically identify and critically assess the clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for the management of critically ill patients with COVID-19 with the AGREE II instrument.
elements.reason: Objective is explicitly stated but no question-formulation framework is mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
The review assesses clinical practice guidelines, not intervention effects, based on the stated objective and evidence.

elements.quote: Selection criteria For inclusion, CPGs had to provide specific recommendations for clinical management, diagnosis and/or treatment of critically ill patients with COVID-19. When more than one version was available, we included only the most updated version or edition of the eligible RGs.
elements.reason: Specifies study design (CPGs) and population, but does not explicitly mention settings, follow-up requirements, or question-framework components.

elements.quote: When more than one version was available, we included only the most updated version or edition of the eligible RGs.
elements.reason: Publication status specified, but dissemination year and language restrictions not explicitly stated in methods; language mentioned in discussion as no restrictions.
The review focuses on guideline quality assessment, and eligibility is based on document type and content, not on outcomes measurement or reporting as in primary studies.
Synthesis groups are not specified in the methods section; groups mentioned in discussion are not linked to objectives.
No rationales provided for the eligibility restrictions, such as including only the most updated version.

elements.quote: An electronic database search was conducted from November 1, 2019 to October 1, 2020 by a health sciences librarian (LH) in Medline (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCO), Embase, China national knowledge infrastructure (CNKI), China Biomedical Literature database (CBM), and WanFang Data... Grey literature search (e.g., CPG databases and repositories and official websites of relevant critical care or intensive care professional societies as a part of snowballing) was conducted across more than 20 different resources and was extended until November 30, 2020.
elements.reason: Dates for electronic database and grey literature searches are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Medline (OVID), CINAHL (EBSCO), Embase, China national knowledge infrastructure (CNKI), China Biomedical Literature database (CBM), and WanFang Data

elements.quote: We extracted the following variables from each eligible CPG: ID (acronym or first author), country, economic classification, healthcare system, scope of the CPG, language, methods of development, date of publication, developer organization (if applicable), type of organization, target critical disease (specialty), CPG implementation tools, consideration of patients' views and preferences, the use of specific method to assess quality of the evidence (e.g. GRADE), and all options of therapeutic interventions for critically ill people with COVID-19 whether general supportive care or specific COVID-19 therapy, results of the AGREE II quality assessments
elements.reason: Variables are listed, but definitions are provided only for some (e.g., ID, developer organization), while others lack explicit definitions.

elements.quote: This rapid and living systematic review was informed by three methodological guides for CPGs' systematic reviews, rapid reviews, and living reviews [ 8 , 19 , 20 ].
elements.reason: Methodological guides are cited as informing the review, which includes the determination of data items to collect.

elements.quote: with the AGREE II instrument
elements.reason: Tool specified but version not explicitly mentioned.

elements.quote: which consists of 23 items grouped in 6 domains, in addition to 2 final overall assessments. The six AGREE II domains are scope and purpose, stakeholder involvement, rigour of development, clarity of presentation, applicability, and editorial independence.
elements.reason: Domains and items assessed by the risk-of-bias tool are specified.

elements.quote: A final overall assessment includes the rating of the overall quality of the CPG (OA1) and whether the CPG would be recommended for use in practice (OA2). The scoring or rating of each CPG was performed using a 7-point Likert scale and a comments section.
elements.reason: Overall risk-of-bias judgement was made and rules for deriving it are reported.

elements.quote: Two reviewers conducted independent quality assessment of each eligible CPG... Discrepancies in the scoring were resolved by focus group discussions facilitated by a CPG methodologist (YSA).
